ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: According to <image1> “Development and Evolution Model Diagram of a Typical Hollowed-out Village in the Urban-Rural Fringe,” what does residential land change rate curve b in the figure represent?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The image shows an evolution curve chart with “time” as the horizontal axis and “residential land change rate” as the vertical axis, and there are three residential land change rate curves a, b, and c in the figure. b is marked beside a curve in the upper right of the figure. This curve as a whole shows staged fluctuations: during the village development process, it once obviously dipped below the zero-change rate, reflecting a period of residential land idling and decline, and then rose again. Combining with the stem’s statement that in urban-rural transformation, population out-migration causes “people leaving and houses becoming empty,” original residential land is abandoned and left idle, forming village hollowing-out; the position where this kind of original residential land is most easily abandoned and declines is usually the old-house concentrated area inside the village, that is, the village center. Therefore, curve b in the figure represents the village center.
